a car park

a forest

questions.questionText:
An economics graduate chooses to work in a bank rather than teach economics which was the
next best alternative.
Which cost is incurred as a result of this decision?

options.text: external cost
internal cost
opportunity cost
private cost

questions.questionText: What is an example of microeconomics?

options.text: a fall in the cost of growing wheat
a fall in the unemployment rate
an increase in the rate of inflation
an increase in government spending

Total revenue falls continuously.

whether consumer or industrial goods are produced

questions.questionText:
The price elasticity of demand for smartphones is believed to be −2.0. A manufacturer decides to
cut prices by 10%.
What will be the effect of this change in price?

options.text: demand will fall by 20%
demand will rise by 5%
quantity supplied will remain unchanged
revenue will increase

questions.questionText: What is a characteristic of a market economic system?

options.text: consumers decide whether production is labour-intensive or capital-intensive
factors of production are government-owned
high levels of government intervention
land and capital are privately owned

questions.questionText:
A government intends to build a new road through a forest.
What will be an external cost of this?

options.text: the cost of building the road
the loss suffered by those who would have used the forest
the cost of maintaining the road
the new jobs created from the construction of the road

questions.questionText: Which function does a central bank provide for the general public?

options.text: accepting deposits
issuing banknotes
making loans
providing overdrafts

questions.questionText:
In some countries, there has been a significant reduction in the number of trade union members.
Who are the members of trade unions?

options.text: employers
exporters
importers
workers

questions.questionText: What would be most likely to encourage a firm to grow internally?

options.text: when diseconomies of scale occur at low levels of output
when economies of scale occur at high levels of output
when new firms enter the market and increase competition
when the firm only supplies the local market

questions.questionText: What is the definition of a government budget?

options.text: a forecast of government spending and revenue for the following financial year
an account of government taxation revenues for the current financial year
an estimate of government capital spending for the current financial year
an explanation of government spending for the following financial year

questions.questionText:
A government decides to increase defence expenditure and reduce direct taxes.
Which type of policy is this?

options.text: exchange rate policy
fiscal policy
monetary policy
trade protection policy

questions.questionText:
Governments use monetary policy such as increasing the rate of interest.
What is a result of increasing the rate of interest?

options.text: It creates disincentives for wage earners.
It discourages investment by entrepreneurs.
It reduces the disposable income of consumers.
It reduces government transfer payments.

questions.questionText: Which government intervention would increase the geographic mobility of labour?

options.text: controlling firms locating in areas of low employment
giving grants to firms moving into areas of high unemployment
providing relocation expenses for workers
subsidising declining industries

questions.questionText: Which action by employers is most likely to reduce long-term economic growth?

options.text: allowing workers time off to attend retraining courses
encouraging workers to work flexibly in different roles
granting workers regular short breaks during the working day
replacing skilled workers with semi-skilled workers
